    Construction

    One- or two-piece solid body, 2 in (the same as the C-75), on the C-75 body as Chuck modelled it: 5/8 in flat bevels on the top and back, leaving a 3/4 in square band round the side, and the middle of the tail left square. Machined in two setups on a 3-axis router (top, then flipped for the back), with a 1/4 in ball-nose for the bevels.

    Bolt-on 25.5 in neck in a standard Fender-pattern pocket meeting the body at the 16th fret: a custom maple neck (21 frets, 12 in radius, ebony board) with the C-75's 11.2° tilt-back Juris headstock and volute, so no string tree is needed; truss rod adjusts through a slot above the nut, under a rosewood cover engraved JURIS; the nickel-silver insignia sits flush in the face and an asset tag is riveted to the back, as on the C-75; Grover 3+3. Classic T layout with no pickguard: vintage T bridge pickup on its baseplate in a 3-saddle plate with strings through the body, a Lollar Gold Foil Soapbar in the neck position (black case, nickel grille over the gold foil, two screws into a P-90 soapbar route on springs), and a 5-1/2 in control plate with 3-way switch, volume and tone, set parallel to the treble bevel. Electrosocket jack on the treble side of the lower bout, where the C-75 has it, with the bevels running unbroken past it.
